schema_ddl:
CREATE TABLE PRODUCT (
    PRODUCT_ID INT,
    PRODUCT_NAME VARCHAR(255),
    UNIT_PRICE INT,
    PRIMARY KEY (PRODUCT_ID),
    CHECK (UNIT_PRICE > 0)
);

CREATE TABLE SALES (
    PRODUCT_ID INT,
    SELLER_ID INT,
    BUYER_ID INT,
    SALE_DATE DATE,
    QUANTITY INT,
    PRICE INT,
    FOREIGN KEY (PRODUCT_ID) REFERENCES PRODUCT(PRODUCT_ID),
    CHECK (QUANTITY > 0),
    CHECK (PRICE > 0)
);
q1: SELECT P.PRODUCT_ID, P.PRODUCT_NAME FROM PRODUCT P INNER JOIN ( SELECT PRODUCT_ID FROM SALES GROUP BY PRODUCT_ID HAVING MIN(SALE_DATE) >= '2019-01-01' AND MAX(SALE_DATE) <= '2019-03-31' ) S ON (P.PRODUCT_ID = S.PRODUCT_ID)
q2: SELECT S.PRODUCT_ID, P.PRODUCT_NAME FROM PRODUCT P RIGHT JOIN SALES S ON P.PRODUCT_ID = S.PRODUCT_ID GROUP BY S.PRODUCT_ID HAVING MIN(S.SALE_DATE) >= '2019-01-01' AND MAX(S.SALE_DATE) <= '2019-03-31'
q1_prompt_sql: SELECT P.PRODUCT_ID, P.PRODUCT_NAME FROM PRODUCT P INNER JOIN ( SELECT PRODUCT_ID FROM SALES GROUP BY PRODUCT_ID HAVING MIN(SALE_DATE) >= '2019-01-01' AND MAX(SALE_DATE) <= '2019-03-31' ) S ON (P.PRODUCT_ID = S.PRODUCT_ID)
q2_prompt_sql: SELECT S.PRODUCT_ID, P.PRODUCT_NAME FROM PRODUCT P RIGHT JOIN SALES S ON P.PRODUCT_ID = S.PRODUCT_ID GROUP BY S.PRODUCT_ID HAVING MIN(S.SALE_DATE) >= '2019-01-01' AND MAX(S.SALE_DATE) <= '2019-03-31'
explanation: Q1 and Q2 are not semantically equivalent. Q1 selects products that have all sales occurring between '2019-01-01' and '2019-03-31', using a subquery on SALES. Q2 performs a RIGHT JOIN from SALES to PRODUCT, then groups by product and applies the same HAVING condition. However, Q2 may return products even if they have no sales within the date range if there are sales outside the range but other sales inside the range. Q1 only includes products that have sales within the date range, while Q2 may return products with some sales inside the range.
counterexample_dsp: A product with sales on '2018-12-31' and '2019-01-15' will be included in Q2 (MIN and MAX across all sales) but not in Q1 (subquery only includes sales within date range). Q1 only returns products where all sales are within the date range, while Q2 returns products that have at least one sale within the date range.
